name: Shebuel
overview: Shebuel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically noted as a descendant of Gershom, the son of Moses. He held the unique role of an officer over the treasures, indicating a position of responsibility within the Levitical service. His lineage and duties emphasize his involvement in the sacred duties assigned to the Levites.
namesAndTitles: The name Shebuel, also recorded as Shubael, likely means 'captive of God' or 'God restores,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God's power and care. These names, while not explicitly given by God, reveal a connection to divine restoration or possession.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Shebuel as a descendant of Gershom, son of Moses, establishing his Levitical heritage. It is also inferred that his father was Jehdeiah, though this is not directly stated. Beyond these, no additional family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Shebuel's significance lies in his role as a Levitical officer charged with overseeing the treasures, a task that required trustworthiness and dedication to the service of the tabernacle or temple. His descent from Gershom, Moses' son, connects him to the foundational leadership of Israel and highlights the continuation of faithful service within the priestly tribe. Through him, the biblical narrative underscores the importance of faithful stewardship in the worship life of God's people.
